headline: COPPER CRASHES 2.5% TO $6.33 — IRAN ESCALATION AND CHILE MINE SHUTDOWNS WHIPSAW METAL STILL UP 12% IN 2026
snippet: COMEX September copper fell as much as 2.5% to $6.33/lb — about 5% below June's all-time record — as two simultaneous shocks hit the market on July 24-25: expanded U.S. airstrikes on Iran pushed Brent above $100/barrel and raised rate-hike-via-inflation fears, while a rare polar atmospheric river system struck central Chile shutting Codelco's El Teniente surface operations, suspending Lundin Mining's Caserones (power cut, access blocked July 18), and curtailing activity at Antofagasta's Los Pelambres and Anglo American's Los Bronces — collectively representing approximately 1.6 million tonnes of temporarily disrupted annual capacity. The paradox traders are navigating: both events are structurally copper-bullish in the medium term (Iran = widening COMEX-LME tariff arb; Chile storm = reduced near-term supply into an already tight physical market), but the simultaneous rate-hike-via-energy-inflation signal caused short-term equity and futures liquidation. Despite the pullback, copper still ended the week higher — and with Teck and Freeport-McMoRan reporting record Q2 earnings this week, the fundamentals-vs-sentiment gap is as wide as it has been all year. Historically, Chile storm disruptions have resolved within 2-4 weeks; the physical tightening thesis remains intact.

headline: THE FED MEETS JULY 29. GOLD SAYS HOLD IS PRICED IN. SILVER SAYS SOMETHING ELSE. — GOLDSILVER.COM FOMC COUNTDOWN
snippet: GoldSilver.com's weekend FOMC countdown analysis argues that gold's price action heading into Tuesday's July 29 Fed decision reflects a rate hold already priced in — gold has held the $4,000–$4,060 range for six consecutive sessions despite CME FedWatch hike odds climbing from 12.8% to 37.9%. Silver is telling a different story: it has been more volatile, fell harder than gold on each hike-scare headline, and sits at an unusually wide discount to its LBMA 2026 consensus target of $79.57/oz — more than 26% upside from current $58. The article frames July 29 as a binary with asymmetric payoff: a hold releases silver's pent-up industrial demand premium (sixth consecutive supply deficit, 46.3 Moz per the Silver Institute); a hike compresses silver further but is already partially priced in given the volatility, while gold's $4,000 support enjoys a central bank bid floor. The gold-silver ratio at 70:1 — its highest in more than a year — amplifies the payoff math: at any gold level above $4,000, ratio normalization to the historical 50:1 average returns silver to $80 without any gold move at all. For junior silver producers and explorers, the current ratio extreme has historically been followed by silver outperforming gold by 2-3x on any macro tailwind.

headline: TECK Q2: EBITDA TRIPLES TO C$2.2B, COPPER OUTPUT UP 25% — RECORD 61% MARGIN VALIDATES JUNIOR COPPER THESIS
snippet: Teck Resources Ltd. (TSX: TECK.B, NYSE: TECK) reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of C$2.2 billion on July 23 — more than triple the prior-year period — at a record 61% EBITDA margin, with copper production rising 25% year-over-year to 135,900 tonnes across QB2, Highland Valley, Carmen de Andacollo, and Antamina. Adjusted EPS of C$1.93 beat consensus of C$1.15 by 68%; revenue of C$3.61 billion exceeded the C$3.3 billion estimate. The copper business alone generated C$1.8 billion in gross profit before D&A — nearly 3x the C$673 million from Q2 2025. Cash flow from operations hit C$1.7 billion; net cash increased by C$756 million during the quarter. Teck maintained 2026 guidance at 455,000–530,000 tonnes copper. For junior copper investors, Teck's margin profile at approximately $6.30/lb copper is the benchmark signal: a senior producer generating C$2.2 billion EBITDA on 25% higher output with a 61% margin illustrates the earnings leverage available across the copper equity space — and the gap between those margins and junior copper valuations on the TSX-V remains historically wide at current spot prices.

headline: FREEPORT Q2: NET INCOME +65%, GRASBERG DOUBLES — COPPER EARNINGS CYCLE PEAKS; SHARES SLIP ON SOFT GUIDANCE
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE: FCX) reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.74 on July 23, beating the $0.62 consensus, on revenue of $7.03 billion (vs. $6.71B expected). Net income attributable to common shareholders hit $984 million — up 65% year-over-year — while the company produced 786 million pounds of copper sold at an average realized price of $6.17/lb. The operational standout: the Grasberg Block Cave in Indonesia doubled copper output as the cave ramp-up reached a new operational phase, while U.S. mines delivered 2.4x more operating income in H1 2026 vs. H1 2025. Freeport cut its 2026 unit net cash cost estimate to $1.90/lb from $1.95/lb and guided H2 copper volumes up more than 20% and H2 gold volumes up over 65% sequentially. Despite the strong beat, shares initially slipped as management maintained conservative copper price assumptions in its guidance framework — a signal the market disagreed with, as the stock recovered. For junior copper project investors: Freeport at $6.17/lb average realized price minus $1.90/lb AISC = $4.27/lb net margin per pound, annualizing to an implied valuation benchmark that still does not appear in junior copper enterprise values.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE Q2 DROPS JULY 29 ON FOMC DAY — HIGHEST-MARGIN GOLD PRODUCER REPORTS INTO MAXIMUM RATE UNCERTAINTY
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd. (TSX: AEM, NYSE: AEM) will release Q2 2026 results after market close on Tuesday, July 29 — the same day as the FOMC rate decision — creating a uniquely event-dense moment for gold mining investors. Management reiterated 2026 production guidance weighted roughly 48%/52% H1/H2, with Q1 production of approximately 825,000 ounces already tracking slightly above plan, and full-year guidance of approximately 3.4 million ounces at all-in sustaining costs of C$1,400–1,550/oz. The confluence of two major market events in one session means Agnico's results will land either into a gold tailwind (Fed holds, gold rallies) or into an immediate headwind (Fed hikes, gold sells off) — with operational execution determining whether the stock amplifies or absorbs the macro move. At $4,052 gold and C$1,500/oz AISC, Agnico's implied net margin is approximately $2,550/oz — the benchmark retail investors should compare against Agnico's market cap and per-ounce resource value when evaluating whether the premium multiple is justified. A management conference call follows July 30 at 11:00 AM EDT.

headline: GLADIATOR EXPANDS YUKON COPPER TO 50,000M — 300M HIGH-GRADE STRIKE; MAIDEN RESOURCE 2026 (TSXV: GLAD)
source_name: North of 60 Mining News / Gladiator Metals
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp. (TSXV: GLAD) confirmed July 24 that high-grade copper-gold-silver continuity at the Cub East discovery now extends more than 300 metres of strike within the Whitehorse Copper Belt, Yukon, prompting a program expansion from 35,000m to 50,000m — funded by a C$35 million placement led by BlackRock. The standout result anchoring the expanded program: hole BCG-035 cut 32 metres grading 1.36% copper and 0.63 g/t gold from 178m depth, including 18 metres at 2.12% Cu and 1.06 g/t Au; companion hole BCG-024 returned 32.7m at 1.06% Cu and 0.44 g/t Au. The consistent widths and multiple high-grade intercepts across 300m of strike suggest a bulk-tonnage skarn or replacement system rather than a narrow vein, improving the feasibility-stage economics profile. Gladiator is advancing Class 3 delineation drilling at the Cowley target to support a maiden NI 43-101 inferred resource estimate in 2026. BlackRock's institutional backing for a Yukon-stage explorer is a notable signal of conviction at a time when copper equity financing is highly selective, and the Whitehorse Copper Belt's infrastructure proximity (municipal power grid, paved highway) is a meaningful discovery-to-development advantage in the current capital environment.

headline: RESOURO FILES MINING CONCESSION AT NOVO MUNDO, BRAZIL — TRIAL OPERATION HEADS TO FULL PRODUCTION LICENSE (ASX: RSM)
snippet: Resouro Strategic Metals Inc. (ASX: RSM) announced July 24 that its wholly owned Brazilian subsidiary lodged a Mining Concession Application on July 16, 2026 for the Novo Mundo Gold Project in Mato Grosso, Brazil (ANM Process No. 866.035/2009) — the key regulatory step under Brazilian mining law that converts an active trial mining operation into a fully licensed, indefinite commercial mining asset. The 930-hectare project sits in the Alta Floresta Gold Province, one of Brazil's most prolific gold-producing regions. CEO Christopher Eager: 'Lodging of the Mining Concession Application is a key regulatory step toward converting our trial mining operation at Novo Mundo into a fully licensed, long-term producing asset.' Brazilian mining concessions typically require 6–24 months for approval from lodgement. Once granted, the concession removes the throughput and operating limitations of trial mining status, enabling Resouro to scale operations to full commercial levels without re-applying for permissions. For ASX investors tracking Resouro's production pathway, this application is the de-risking milestone that separates the project from a development-stage asset and begins the countdown to unrestricted production authorization.

headline: NEXGEN ROOK I CONSTRUCTION BEGINS — C$2.2B, 4-YEAR BUILD FOR 30M LBS/YEAR URANIUM UNDERWAY IN ATHABASCA (TSX: NXE)
snippet: NexGen Energy Ltd. (TSX: NXE, NYSE: NXE) has officially commenced construction on the Rook I Project in the southern Athabasca Basin, Saskatchewan — the C$2.2 billion, four-year build that will bring the world's largest high-grade undeveloped uranium deposit into production. At full capacity, Rook I targets up to 30 million pounds of U3O8 annually, representing more than 20% of current global uranium fuel supply and over 50% of western world supply from a single project. Construction follows the CNSC Site Preparation and Construction Licence issued March 5, 2026 and a subsequent Final Investment Decision. The Arrow deposit — discovered by NexGen in 2014 — is centred on exceptionally high grades in the Athabasca Basin's most established uranium regulatory jurisdiction. For uranium equity investors, Rook I's transition from development-stage to construction-stage removes the largest binary risk (permit and FID) and begins the four-year countdown to production: historically the phase in which uranium developer NAV multiples compress as discount rates apply to a known timeline, while simultaneously attracting a larger class of infrastructure and income-oriented institutional buyers who require construction certainty before allocation.

headline: COBRE PANAMA AUDIT: 88% COMPLIANT — FIRST QUANTUM IN 60-65% STAKE TALKS AS S&P MODELS H2 2026 RESTART (TSX: FM)
snippet: Panama's Ministry of Environment formally completed its independent audit of the suspended Cobre Panama mine (operated by First Quantum Minerals — TSX: FM) and found overall compliance at approximately 88% — with remaining deficiencies in biodiversity management, ecological restoration, and environmental monitoring, but not in core infrastructure or contamination prevention. The result is broadly positive for restart negotiations: an 88% compliance finding gives Panama's government legal and political cover to approve concession discussions without triggering an environmental veto. S&P Global Ratings has incorporated a H2 2026 restart and ramp-up into its base-case scenario. The leading structural model under active negotiation would give First Quantum a 60–65% stake with the Panamanian state holding the balance and owning the mining concession itself — a sovereignty model that appears more politically durable than the prior arrangement. Cobre Panama was producing approximately 350,000 tonnes of copper per year before its November 2023 shutdown; a full restart would represent the single largest addition to global copper supply for 2026–2027, and the potential removal of 350,000 tonnes of currently absent annual supply from a market already approaching COMEX records is a significant reason copper's $6.30/lb floor has held through geopolitical volatility this week.

headline: COBALT +130%, LITHIUM DOUBLED IN 2026 — DRC EXPORT CAPS FORCE BATTERY METALS RECOVERY, BUT THREE FACTORS LIMIT UPSIDE
snippet: Battery metal prices staged a broad 2026 recovery across lithium, cobalt, nickel, and copper, with cobalt surging approximately 130% and lithium more than doubling from its June 2025 trough near ¥59,000/tonne to over ¥130,000+, according to NAI 500's July 2026 analysis. The primary driver for cobalt: the DRC government capped outbound shipments at approximately 96,600 metric tonnes annually for 2026–2027 — roughly half of 2024 peak output — forcing supply braking that has outpaced sluggish downstream EV demand growth. Three structural caps limit the upside runway: (1) Indonesian HPAL nickel supply continues to flood the market regardless of Western EV demand signals; (2) lithium's rally is supply-forced rather than demand-pulled, and Australian and Chinese hard-rock producers are already mobilizing to restore volumes at higher prices; (3) the stop-start EV adoption rate in Europe and the U.S. limits the velocity of battery raw material demand recovery. For junior battery metals developers in stable western jurisdictions — Canada, Australia, Finland — the combination of recovering commodity prices and aggressive domestic critical minerals policy (U.S. IRA, Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy, EU CRM Act) is the most supportive it has been since the 2021–2022 cycle peak, but the path to $130+/tonne lithium carbonate and $25+/lb cobalt is a supply-constrained squeeze, not a demand-driven re-rating.

headline: CAMECO Q2 DUE JULY 31 — CIGAR LAKE BACK AT FULL CAPACITY; LONG-TERM URANIUM AT 18-YEAR HIGH $94/LB (TSX: CCO)
snippet: Cameco Corporation (TSX: CCO, NYSE: CCJ) is expected to report Q2 2026 earnings on July 31 — four days after the FOMC decision — with analyst consensus calling for a year-over-year earnings decline despite a record uranium contracting environment. The apparent paradox: Cameco's revenue is driven by long-term contract prices rather than spot, and the mix of legacy lower-price contracts and newer contracts priced at the 18-year high of $94/lb U3O8 creates a lag effect where spot records don't immediately flow through to income. Q1 2026 baseline: revenue C$845 million (up 7%), net earnings attributable to shareholders C$131 million (up 87%), uranium segment earnings C$358 million. The key operational watch point for Q2: Cigar Lake — which briefly curtailed output during a July shutdown — has returned to full capacity, and any production update from management will be closely watched for full-year guidance implications. The forward earnings trajectory is the real story: as legacy contracts roll over and are replaced at $94/lb, Cameco's 2027–2028 revenue profile is substantially stronger than current market pricing implies, making the Q2 'earnings decline' a potential buying signal rather than a thesis change for investors with a 12–24 month horizon.
